'''''Arnoseris''''' is a [[monotypic]] [[genus]] of flowering plants in the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/37208346#page/411/mode/1up Gaertner, Joseph. 1791.  De Fructibus et Seminibus Plantarum.  2(3): 355] in Latin</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/37208346#page/655/mode/1up Gaertner, Joseph. 1791.  De Fructibus et Seminibus Plantarum.  2(3):plate 157, figure 3] line drawing as illustration</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40019772 Tropicos, ''Arnoseris'' Gaertn.]</ref>

The only known species is  '''''Arnoseris minima''''', native to [[Europe]], [[Morocco]], and the [[Middle East]]; naturalized in parts of northeastern [[North America]] ([[Nova Scotia]], [[New Brunswick]], [[Prince Edward Island]], [[Maine]], [[New Hampshire]], [[Pennsylvania]], [[Ohio]], [[Michigan]]).<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Arnoseris%20minima.png Biota of North America Program 2013 county distribution map]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=arnoseris+minima Altervista Flora Italiana,  ''Arnoseris minima'' (L.) Schweigg. & Korte ] includes photos and European distribution map</ref> Common names in the United States: '''dwarf nipplewort''' or '''lamb-succory'''.<ref>Brako, L., A.Y. Rossman & D.F. Farr. 1995. Scientific and Common Names of 7,000 Vascular Plants in the United States 1–294.</ref> Common names in the British Isles: '''lamb's succory'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref>

It has a maximum height of 30 cm, is herbaceous and does not spread vegetatively.<ref>[https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/arnoseris-minima Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora]</ref>

The species became extinct across the [[British Isles]] in 1971.<ref>[https://www.woodlandtrust.org.uk/blog/2018/05/extinct-and-rare-plants/ Woodland Trust - 7 Extinct Plants in the UK and the Rarest Plants to Save]</ref> There was an attempt to reintroduce the species, and there has been one recent sighting in England.<ref>[https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/arnoseris-minima Online Atlas of the British Flora]</ref>

''Arnoseris minima'' is an annual weed of cornfields and fallow fields, favouring infertile, sandy, acidic soils.<ref>[https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/arnoseris-minima Online Atlas of the British Flora]</ref>

[[File:Arnoseris minima kz04.jpg|thumb|left|''Arnoseris minima'' photographed in Poland in 2008]]
The word 'succory' is an anglicization of the French 'cichorie' ([[chicory]]). The 'lamb' in the name denotes that it is a chicory only suitable for animal consumption.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=1JJHAQAAMAAJ&dq=succory+etymology&pg=PA327 a New Universal Etymological and Pronouncing Dictionary of the English Language]</ref> The genus ''Arnoseris'' comes from the [[Ancient Greek]] 'arnos seris' meaning 'sheep's [[endive]]'. The species epithet ''minima'' means 'small'.<ref>[http://beta.semanticfna.org/wiki/Arnoseris Flora of North America]</ref>

== Secondary metabolites ==
''Arnoseris minima'' is a source of the simple [[coumarin]] [[aesculetin]] and the [[flavonoids]] [[luteolin]], [[luteolin]] 7-O-β-D-glucoside, luteolin 4'-O-β-D-glucoside, and 3-O-methylquercetin.<ref>{{cite journal | year = 2005 | author = Zidorn, C | author2 = Udovičić, V | author3 = Spitaler, R | author4 = Ellmerer, E P | author5 = Stuppner, H | title = Secondary metabolites from ''Arnoseris minima''| volume = 33 | pages = 827–829 | issn = 0305-1978 | journal = Biochemical Systematics and Ecology | issue = 8 | doi = 10.1016/j.bse.2004.12.026| bibcode = 2005BioSE..33..827Z }}</ref>
